summary.headline: AESL FY26 capitalisation of about INR15,300 crores; FY27 capex guided at INR21,000-22,000 crores and capitalisation at INR21,000-22,000 crores.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 as a year of heavy commissioning, led by the Mumbai HVDC project (INR7,000 crores, commissioned 15 March 2026) and 82.29 lakh smart meters installed in the year against a 70 lakh target. Management guided FY27 capex to about INR21,000-22,000 crores (transmission about INR15,500 crores) and FY28 to about INR22,000-25,000 crores, with capitalisation of INR21,000-22,000 crores in FY27 and about INR13,000 crores in FY28. Credit ratings were described as improved to AAA+/AAA for most assets, with interest costs falling, and net leverage is to be held at 4.5x-4.7x. Management declined to give formal EBITDA guidance but said transmission EBITDA could reach about 3x current levels over 36-40 months and that FY27 consolidated EBITDA could be about INR11,500 crores versus INR8,726 crores in FY26 (as stated by the CEO).

segments.name: Transmission
segments.commentary: FY26 capitalisation INR10,260 crores; market share of bids improved to about 29-30% vs 20-25% earlier; FY27 capex guided at about INR15,500 crores, FY28 about INR20,000 crores. Mumbai HVDC (INR7,000 crores) commissioned 15 March 2026 with full-year tariff of about INR1,300 crores to accrue from FY27.

segments.name: Distribution (AEML)
segments.commentary: FY26 capitalisation INR1,511 crores; FY27 capex about INR2,350 crores (FY28 about INR2,000 crores). Distribution EBIT reported down about 14% per analyst question; management says tariffs held flat with efficiency gains passed to returns. RAB has grown from about INR5,400 crores to about INR10,500 crores.

segments.name: Smart metering
segments.commentary: 82.29 lakh meters installed in FY26 (vs 70 lakh target), cumulative about 1 crore; concession book of 2.46 crores meters. FY27 installations guided at minimum 1 crore meters and FY27 capex about INR3,900 crores; FY28 about INR1,500 crores from existing order book.

segments.name: C&I / renewable trading
segments.commentary: About 5,000 MW renewable capacity contracted, of which about 1,400 MW tied up with third-party consumers; margins on tied-up capacity stated above INR0.50 per unit. Detailed C&I presentation deferred to May next year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex about INR21,000-22,000 crores: transmission about INR15,500 crores, distribution about INR2,350 crores, smart metering about INR3,900 crores.
FY28 capex about INR22,000-25,000 crores (transmission about INR20,000 crores, distribution about INR2,000 crores, smart metering about INR1,500 crores plus new orders).
FY27 capitalisation about INR21,000-22,000 crores; FY28 about INR13,000 crores; HVDC projects to commission from FY29.
Net leverage to be maintained at about 4.5x-4.7x; equity portion of asset funding from internal accruals, debt 70:30.
FY27 consolidated EBITDA could be about INR11,500 crores (CEO); transmission EBITDA to reach about 3x current levels within 36-40 months (CFO); management does not formally guide EBITDA.

Transmission bid market share to be maintained at 25-30%, implying about INR40,000-50,000 crores of new transmission opportunity; 12-month tender pipeline about INR80,000-1,00,000 crores, unchanged year on year.
capex_capacity: Mumbai HVDC (INR7,000 crores) fully commissioned on 15 March 2026; Pole 2 under evaluation at MERC and STU level, no commitment yet.
Fatehpur-Bhadla HVDC: construction begun at substation and line level; no significant ROW challenge; percentage completion not disclosed.
Khavda-Olpad HVDC: contracts finalised; Khavda land in possession; Olpad land possession expected from Power Grid in about a month; ROW and forest/environment clearance applications underway.
Locked-in capex of about INR77,000 crores over four years; INR72,000 crores under-construction pipeline in transmission per CFO; CWIP about INR2,500 crores plus non-SCA CWIP about INR2,053 crores.
SCA assets: contracted assets about INR6,200 crores and under-construction about INR7,000 crores (as clarified on call).
demand_pricing: Smart meter concession pool expanded from 2.3 crores to 2.46 crores meters; further 9-10 crores meters of opportunity pending, with Tamil Nadu approved under RDSS and Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and MP parts awaiting tenders.
Intrastate transmission pipeline estimated at about INR30,000-40,000 crores annually across states, with Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka bidding.
Transmission tender pipeline of about INR1.5 trillion identified; management says a large state-level opportunity is emerging.
AEML tariffs held at roughly the same level while efficiency gains accrue to shareholders; AEML rated number one distribution company for four years.
Supply chain: no project delayed due to equipment delivery; GIS, transformer and reactor capacity expanding in India; TBCB bid conditions bar Chinese-manufactured equipment.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 and FY28 capex expectations by business?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR21,000-22,000 crores (transmission 15,500, distribution 2,350, smart metering 3,900); FY28 about INR22,000-25,000 crores (transmission 20,000, distribution 2,000, smart metering 1,500 plus new orders).

qa_highlights.question: How will the FY26 HVDC and capitalisation translate into FY27-28, and how much CWIP reconciles with the transmission capitalisation guide?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capitalisation about INR21,000-22,000 crores and FY28 about INR13,000 crores. Management said heavy equipment procured late in the year is capitalised immediately, so CWIP alone does not explain the INR14,500-15,000 crores transmission capitalisation target.

qa_highlights.question: How should the leverage be viewed given negative free cash flow in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said assets are funded 70:30 debt to equity, with only the equity portion from internal accruals, and the company is comfortable funding existing capex; net leverage to stay at 4.5x-4.7x.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA contribution from FY26 commissioned transmission projects and the win rate in tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR1,600 crores of incremental transmission revenue on full run-rate; win rate improved to close to 30% from 20-25%, with a target band of 25-30%.

qa_highlights.question: How will Mumbai HVDC revenue be booked in FY27, and what is the status of Pole 2?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year tariff about INR1,300 crores to accrue from FY27 once approved by regulator; Pole 2 is still under MERC and STU evaluation with no commitment.

qa_highlights.question: Why did smart meter operating EBITDA figures differ between the nine-month and full-year presentations?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said operating EBITDA is a function of meters installed and there was no restatement; he said the figures would be checked offline as the analyst cited a nine-month figure of INR466 crores that did not reconcile.

qa_highlights.question: Can operating profit double or triple, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said FY27 consolidated EBITDA could be about INR11,500 crores; CFO said transmission EBITDA could reach about 3x current levels in 36-40 months, with distribution EBITDA about INR2,500 crores rising to INR3,000-3,200 crores and smart metering EBITDA INR2,400-3,000 crores once fully built.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin on the 1.5 GW C&I trading book?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins on tied-up capacity are above INR0.50 per unit; the rest is being worked on, and sales are currently merchant with more certainty expected after contracts.

risks_watch: Negative free cash flow of roughly INR7,500 crores in FY26 (operating cash flow about INR10,000-11,000 crores vs capex INR14,431 crores) and the path to borrowings given capex of about INR77,000 crores over four years.
Right-of-way challenges from landowners and the timing of Khavda-Olpad and Fatehpur-Bhadla construction starts.
Mumbai HVDC Pole 2 approval at MERC and STU level remains uncertain.
Smart meter tender timing for pending states, which management says may follow state elections.
Distribution EBIT reported down about 14% year on year despite higher volumes; FY27 distribution profitability is not guided.
Discrepancy between nine-month and full-year smart meter operating EBITDA figures raised by an analyst and left for offline follow-up.
Win rate and capital discipline in transmission bidding, limited to 25-30% market share.

summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on execution, smart-meter delivery and credit ratings, and on transmission growth. Cautious and evasive on hard numbers: management declined to give formal EBITDA guidance, left the smart-meter EBITDA discrepancy for offline follow-up, and did not give a 4-year borrowing figure.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 capex of INR21,000-22,000 crore and capitalisation of the same size, backed by the Mumbai HVDC commissioning (INR7,000 crore), 1 crore smart meter installs, and a locked-in pipeline of about INR77,000 crore; FY27 consolidated EBITDA of about INR11,500 crore (vs INR8,726 crore in FY26) is stated by the CEO, though no formal EBITDA guidance is given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 consolidated EBITDA could be about INR11,500 crores vs INR8,726 crores in FY26 (about +32%), with Mumbai HVDC full-year tariff of about INR1,300 crores accruing from FY27 and about INR1,600 crores transmission run-rate add from FY26 projects; management declined formal EBITDA guidance.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: FY26 capitalisation about INR15,300 crores with Mumbai HVDC (INR7,000 crores) commissioned 15 March 2026, and FY27 capitalisation guided at INR21,000-22,000 crores with about INR77,000 crores locked-in capex over four years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Smart meter installs guided at minimum 1 crore in FY27 vs 82.29 lakh in FY26 (+~22%), and transmission bid share held at 25-30% against a 12-month tender pipeline of INR80,000-1,00,000 crores.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex guided at INR21,000-22,000 crores and FY28 at INR22,000-25,000 crores, with Fatehpur-Bhadla and Khavda-Olpad HVDC projects in construction or contracting stages and a 25-30% bid share target implying INR40,000-50,000 crores of new transmission opportunity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says transmission bid share improved to about 29-30% from 20-25%, but formal EBITDA guidance is withheld, so any raise would depend on Pole 2 approval and HVDC tariff accrual from FY27.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY26 free cash flow was about negative INR7,500 crores, distribution EBIT fell about 14%, Pole 2 approval is uncertain, and smart meter tender timing for pending states may slip after state elections.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: C&I/renewable trading has about 5,000 MW contracted with about 1,400 MW tied to third-party consumers at margins above INR0.50 per unit, but the detailed C&I presentation is deferred to May next year.

rows.label: Smart meter concession pool and pending state tenders
rows.why: Concession book at 2.46 crore meters with 9-10 crore meters of further opportunity, and FY28 smart metering capex of about INR1,500 crores from the existing order book plus new orders.

rows.label: Net leverage held at 4.5x-4.7x while capex ramps
rows.why: Management committed to 4.5x-4.7x net leverage with assets funded 70:30 debt-equity, while FY27 capex of INR21,000-22,000 crores far exceeds FY26 operating cash flow of about INR10,000-11,000 crores.

rows.label: Mumbai HVDC Pole 2 approval
rows.why: Pole 2 is under MERC and STU evaluation with no commitment yet, and approval would extend the HVDC revenue base beyond the INR1,300 crores full-year tariff.

tone.note: Management was confident on execution, smart-meter delivery (82.29 lakh vs 70 lakh target), credit ratings and transmission growth, but cautious on hard numbers: no formal EBITDA guidance, smart-meter EBITDA discrepancy left for offline follow-up, and no 4-year borrowing figure.
